svg.title: ccTLD registry hijacks on .gh, .sl and .as - authoritative DNS takeover, domain-validated certificates for Google names, CT detection
svg.desc: Two-lane kill chain. Left lane, the target side: 1 third-party ccTLD registry operators compromised by an unpublished method, 2 authoritative DNS records changed for Google and YouTube names under .gh, .sl and .as, 3 public CAs validate control through attacker DNS and issue wildcard certificates, 4 the certificates appear in Certificate Transparency logs on 2026-09-22, 09-25 and 09-27, 5 a window of possible interception that is not established, 6 Google detects, Chrome blocks with CRLSets and CAs revoke, 7 residual risk from cached validation and non-Chrome clients. Stages 1 to 3 and 7 are critical. Right lane, the public record: what is unknown, the seven names, issuers, the count conflict between 12 and 32 certificates, detection anchors and hardening, with the related eMudhra intermediate CA key weakness. Detection anchors are CT monitoring, delegation and CAA drift, exposure queries for the window and non-Google issuers on Google-brand names.
svg.text: ccTLD registry hijacks (.gh, .sl, .as): DNS takeover and rogue certificates
Vendors: Google Chrome team, THN, iTnews, BleepingComputer - Date: 2026-10-21 - Cluster: Unattributed - Day 120
TARGET SIDE: REGISTRIES, DOMAIN OWNERS, CAs, CLIENTS
PUBLIC RECORD, GAPS AND DEFENDER VIEW
Third-party ccTLD registry operators compromised
Registries for .gh, .sl and .as; operators not named
Initial access method not published
Admin or EPP path suspected (vendor inference only)
Google 2026-10-06; no actor named
Authoritative DNS changed for Google names
Delegation or records for google.com.gh, youtube.sl, google.as
Names resolve to infrastructure the actor controls
Hijack dates at the registry are not published
Hunt H2 KQL k3 Sigma 03
Public CAs validate through attacker DNS
Domain control validation passes against hijacked zone
Wildcard DV certificates from Lets Encrypt and ZeroSSL
CAs not at fault, per Google; DCV method not published
Sigma 04 Suricata 6370003-6370006
Certificates logged in Certificate Transparency
Most certificates per ccTLD within about 90 minutes
At least 12 (THN) or 32 (iTnews): conflict, not reproduced
CT log, crt.sh, CertSpotter
Hunt H1 YARA 2 rules
Window of possible interception (not established)
Valid certificate plus attacker IP means a valid-looking page
No source shows traffic was intercepted or abused
Exposure window: 2026-09-22 to 2026-10-01
T1557 not established
KQL k1 Sigma 01-02 Suricata 6370001-2 H3
Detection and response: Google, Chrome and CAs
Google aware the week before its 2026-10-06 post
Chrome CRLSet block; 3 certs revoked 09-26, 9 on 10-01
CT review found other brands; owners told where possible
CRLSet revocation CPR
Chrome users need no action
Residual risk after the zone is restored
Cached DCV can allow issuance after control returns
CAA is a DNS record: it cannot stop an active hijack
Non-Chrome clients and apps are not covered by CRLSets
RFC 8659 RFC 8657 SC-081v3
Hunt H2 registry lock DNSSEC
A
What is NOT public
No actor, alias or country attribution
No nameservers, IP addresses or registry operator names
No entry method into the registries; no CVE
No hashes or files: nothing to scan on endpoints
Repo IOC feed: no network IOC
Source: Google blog, BleepingComputer
B
The seven named hostnames (legitimate Google sites)
google.com.gh youtube.com.gh (.gh, 2026-09-22)
google.sl google.com.sl youtube.sl (.sl, 2026-09-25)
google.as youtube.as (.as, 2026-09-27)
Do not blocklist: use for exposure scoping only
Sigma 01-02 YARA Suricata 6370001-2
Source: THN CT analysis
C
Issuers and validation as reported
THN: Lets Encrypt 11, ZeroSSL 1 (DV, 12 certificates)
iTnews: wildcards at LE and ZeroSSL, 1 Cloudflare CA cert
CAA on all seven names on 10-07 pointed to pki.goog
CAs not accused; validation method not published
Issuer not GTS on Google-brand SNI = lead
D
Source conflicts, kept unresolved
12 certificates (THN) versus 32 (iTnews): scope differs
iTnews guess about a Cloudflare account is unconfirmed
Security Arsenal rules are vendor inference, untested
Registry hijack dates: none; certificate dates only
See README conflict table
Sources read as page summaries
E
Detection anchors in this folder
CT monitoring of the whole portfolio (hunt H1)
Delegation, NS and CAA drift from outside (hunt H2)
Exposure window review for users and apps (hunt H3)
Non-Google issuer on Google-brand SNI (Suricata)
Sigma 01-04 KQL k1-k3 YARA 2 rules
Suricata sids 6370001-6370006
F
Hardening and a related CA incident
Registry lock, DNSSEC, strict CAA with RFC 8657 binding
Shorter certificate and DCV reuse lifetimes (SC-081v3)
Related: eMudhra intermediate CA keys, weak randomness
CRLSet 2026-10-17; root removal expected 2026-10-27
Not the same incident: no certs seen in CT
Source: Google blog 2026-10-20
Detection anchors: CT issuance, delegation and CAA drift, exposure window, non-Google issuer on Google-brand SNI
Rules in this folder: Sigma 01-04, KQL k1-k3, YARA 2 rules, Suricata sids 6370001-6370006, PEAK hunts H1-H3.
No sample, no CVE, no actor, no network IOC: the evidence is DNS state and certificates. Counts and dates are press readings of CT data.
Act: monitor CT for every domain incl. parked ccTLDs, publish strict CAA, lock registrar and registry accounts, scope exposure 09-22 to 10-01.
